Done. I diagnosed the problem against the real repo (cloned `wojons/ai_plays_poke`, examined the fix commit `0f35360`) and wrote the self-contained solution to `/home/kara/solution.md`.

## Verification performed
- **Confirmed the repo checkout is at the fix** (`0f35360` HEAD) and read the complete diff.
- **Root cause confirmed:** `test_integration.py` is only ~10.2s; the real cost was the *unmarked* heavy classes (network retry/backoff, memory/perf benchmarks, RAM scan, mode-duration) that `-m "not integration"` couldn't exclude because they carried no marker.
- **Marker registration verified** in `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options].markers` — both `slow` and `integration` are declared, and a scan of all `@pytest.mark.*` usage across `tests/` shows only builtins (`skip`, `skipif`, `parametrize`) and registered markers (`slow`, `integration`, `live_api`, `rom`), so `--strict-markers` collection won't fail.
- **Full change mapped** file-by-file (class-level `@pytest.mark.slow` for retry/perf/RAM/mode classes; function-level `@pytest.mark.slow` for isolated slow tests in `test_ai_client.py`; class-level `@pytest.mark.integration` for component-flow classes; README command updated to `-m "not integration and not slow"`).

Note: I could not execute the full test run in the sandbox (missing Python deps like `pyboy`/`openai` cause a collection-time import failure unrelated to this fix). The solution therefore cites the measured numbers from the problem/commit (`3825 passed / 8 skipped / 62 deselected in ~68s`, full suite `3881 passed / 14 skipped in ~180s`) and includes the exact markers, commands, a measurement-first step (`--durations=25`), and a check-list covering the `-k gameplay` / registration pitfalls.

signatures.description: A documented pytest 'fast subset' command (e.g. -m 'not integration') takes >90s and barely progresses, because heavy test classes run UNMARKED so the exclusion marker excludes nothing. Solved 2026-08-16 in ai_plays_poke (GAP-026, commit 0f35360): root cause was NOT the obvious integration file (tests/test_integration.py was only 10.2s of the suite) but OTHER unmarked heavy tests (network retry/backoff classes ~12s each, memory/performance benchmarks ~11s, RAM scanning ~9s, mode-duration ~9s, API retry tests). Fix: measure first (pytest --durations or timing), then mark ALL heavy classes with @pytest.mark.slow (class-level for retry/perf classes, function-level for isolated slow tests) plus @pytest.mark.integration for component-flow classes; document the combined command .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q -m 'not integration and not slow' with measured runtimes in README. Result: 3825 passed/8 skipped/62 deselected in 68s (85s under host load), full suite unchanged 3881 passed/14 skipped in ~180s. Pitfall: a '-k gameplay' alternative does NOT work when slow tests are not gameplay-marked; verify the marker registration exists in pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options].
